coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Skip the long run. Your recovery score is 0/100 and resting HR jumped 9 bpm above your 30-day average—your system is compromised. With 3h45m of fragmented sleep last night, a 15–18 mile Saturday would be destructive, not adaptive. Instead: 6–8 easy miles at Z2 (130–140 bpm, well below your recent 142–154 avg), flat terrain, no vert work. This protects your 48-day window to race and keeps you from digging a deeper hole. You've logged 10 miles this week already; quality over volume in taper.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your body is running a sleep deficit and elevated baseline stress—treat today as a recovery fuel day, not a high-burn day. Prioritize: 1.2g carb per kg bodyweight spread across meals (aim for 90–120g today), adequate protein (25–30g per meal) to support HRV recovery, and sodium to restore plasma volume. Skip the temptation to load extra carbs because you're 'tapering'; instead, eat normally and trust your glycogen stores. Hydrate aggressively—your elevated resting HR suggests mild dehydration contributing to the red recovery score.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your immediate bottleneck. Last night's 3h45m at 28.6% efficiency is unacceptable this close to race day—you need 8+ hours to reverse the HRV suppression and lower that resting HR back to 65. Tonight: no screens after 21:00, cool room (≤65°F), consider a magnesium glycinate 300–400mg 90 min before bed. If travel or work stress is driving the insomnia, block it now—48 days out, one bad sleep night spirals into two, then three. This is non-negotiable.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the hardest part of taper: feeling weak while the race looms. That easy 6–8 miles today will feel slow and boring—that's the point. Your nervous system is cooked; the Julian Alps demands a calm, recovered nervous system more than it demands one more hard session. Use this run to confirm your legs feel light and your HR doesn't spike unnaturally. If your resting HR hasn't dropped 3–4 bpm by Thursday, we discuss whether you need an extra recovery day. Trust the taper design.
